It is pertinent to note that even as per the DAR filed by the investigating officer, accident has occurred at the crossing where a traffic light was also installed.
As per the DAR, the petitioner contributed to the accident by being negligent in keeping to the left side of the road and by maintaining an excessive speed.
Petitioner has failed to produce his driving licence to rebut the plea of riding a motorcycle without holding a valid driving licence.

At the same time, it has been held in Dinesh Kumar v. National Insurance Company Ltd.(2018) 1 SCC 750 that mere absence of driving licence with the injured or deceased would not amount to contributory negligence.
Further, since there is no evidence to show that the petitioner either jumped the red light or was at an excessively high speed, no contributory negligence qua such plea can be assumed.
Further, since the accident has taken place at almost the center point of a junction, it cannot be said that the petitioner failed to keep on his left side.
As such, no deduction can be made on the ground of contributory negligence.

Since no statutory defence has been raised by the insurance company, insurance company is liable to compensate the petitioner.

18. As regards loss of earning of petitioner, it first needs to be ascertained the nature of job and salary/wages drawn by petitioner at the time of accident.
Petitioner has claimed to be working as a driver at the time of accident and drawing a salary of Rs.15,000/-p.m.,however no evidence has been lead to prove his employment or salary.
No proof of educational qualification or even a driving licence, to prove that he could have worked as a driver has been produced.
As such, income of the injured has to be assessed as per minimum wages of an unskilled labour.

Having regard to the medical documents showing the period of hospitalization and the nature of injury suffered, it is assumed that the petitioner may have been incapacitated from working for at least one month.
Accordingly, petitioner is entitled to compensation towards loss of income for one month.
As per minimum wages of an unskilled labour at Delhi, at the time of accident were Rs.13,896/-.
Hence, the same is granted towards loss of income.
He is also entitled to attendant charges for the said period i.e. Rs.10,000/-.
No compensation towards future loss of income can be granted in cases where petitioner has not proved to have sustained any permanent disability.
